guide.electron.title: Electron · Engineering Handbook
guide.electron.first_light.title: Your first light
guide.electron.first_light.subtitle: 01 / A closed loop
guide.electron.first_light.p0: Place a hand-crank supply, 220 ohm resistor and LED on top of a smooth-stone bench. Face the terminals upward for your first circuit.
guide.electron.first_light.p1: Use the spool to connect supply + to resistor A, resistor B to LED +, and LED minus back to supply minus.
guide.electron.first_light.p2: Use the supply with an empty hand. One crank per second adds 5 J, up to 200 J. Reversed LEDs and circuits without a return wire do not light.
guide.electron.first_light.p3: The supply produces 5 V with internal resistance. Connecting an LED directly causes overcurrent and eventually destroys it.
guide.electron.wiring.title: Several wires in one block
guide.electron.wiring.subtitle: 02 / Straight first + automatic routing
guide.electron.wiring.p0: A spool starts with 16 blocks of wire. Click a pin or surface to select a start, then any target to connect. A new surface node costs 1/16 block. Aligned points use a straight run; diagonal targets and obstacles use routing.
guide.electron.wiring.p1: Place intermediate nodes to choose where a route passes. Aim to preview, then click to connect. A component pin ends the chain; clicking the current node also finishes. Failed connections consume nothing and leave no partial tap.
guide.electron.wiring.p2: Click any existing wire midway to make a branch. Its color and total paid length are preserved. Different colors can join explicitly; simply crossing does not short them.
guide.electron.wiring.p3: Wire follows exposed corners and steps, up to 32 blocks per run. Components can sit on a bench. Only power cable can span complete tower terminals, up to 64 blocks; walls require ports.
guide.electron.wall_ports.title: Through a solid wall
guide.electron.wall_ports.subtitle: 03 / Two-core wall ports
guide.electron.wall_ports.p0: Use a wall port on any face of an ordinary solid block. The wall remains intact and two independent contacts appear on the opposite face.
guide.electron.wall_ports.p1: Copper is core 0 and silver is core 1. Both sides connect 0 to 0 and 1 to 1. Use one for supply and one for return; they are separate conductors.
guide.electron.wall_ports.p2: A wall block has four mounting corners. Overlapping cores are refused. Thick walls need a port in each block; aligned adjacent contacts join matching cores.
guide.electron.wall_ports.p3: Containers, machines and bedrock cannot be drilled. Removing the wall disconnects and recovers attachments. Blocks carrying wiring or ports cannot currently be pushed by pistons.
guide.electron.measurement.title: Multimeter and measurement HUD
guide.electron.measurement.subtitle: Live readings in survival require an instrument
guide.electron.measurement.p0: 1  Tooltips retain rated specifications and wiring instructions. In survival, holding or using a device does not reveal live voltage, current, resistance or stored energy; battery items also hide their live charge bar. Creative mode permits diagnostic readings. Light, motion and battery panel indicators remain visible physical states.
guide.electron.measurement.p1: 2  Hold the multimeter and select two terminals: COM first, then the probe. The bottom-right HUD continuously shows their voltage difference. Sneak-use a device to read its current and state, or a wire to read branch current. Putting the meter away hides the HUD.
guide.electron.measurement.p2: 3  Use in air to clear probes; sneak-use in air toggles V / Ω. Resistance mode measures the equivalent resistance between the probes, including parallel paths. Powered sources or charged capacitors block resistance measurement. Disconnect and discharge first; open circuits and out-of-range values show OL.
guide.electron.measurement.p3: 4  The server calculates readings and sends them only to the player holding the meter, with regular refreshes. Unavailable, unloaded or paused targets do not retain stale values. Voltage probes need a common circuit reference. A device voltage rating is not a live measurement.
guide.electron.logic.title: Two logic gate families
guide.electron.logic.subtitle: 05 / Redstone and electrical wiring
guide.electron.logic.p0: Redstone models have red boards and redstone contacts. Eight gate functions and the binary memory keep vanilla redstone interfaces. The arrow marks the output.
guide.electron.logic.p1: Electrical models have green panels and five terminals. VCC takes 5 V and GND the return. A/B are inputs; Y is the output. NOT and BUFFER do not use B.
guide.electron.logic.p2: Electrical gates need power. Input at or below 30% of supply is 0 and at or above 70% is 1. Intermediate or floating input is X. No power gives Z; neither X nor Z is a valid 0.
guide.electron.logic.p3: Electrical gates have a two-tick delay, input impedance, idle consumption and limited output current. Do not drive motors directly or short the output to a supply rail.
guide.electron.crafting.title: Materials and crafting
guide.electron.crafting.subtitle: 06 / Starter workshop
guide.electron.crafting.p0: The starter recipes use a vanilla crafting table or the assembly table 3x3 grid. The main mod does not require the calculator generator.
guide.electron.crafting.p1: Spool: two copper, two paper, a stick and two planks. Hand-crank supply: two copper, two iron, redstone and a lever.
guide.electron.crafting.p2: Resistors: two copper and two bricks, with coal for 100 ohm, charcoal for 220 ohm or quartz for 1 kilohm. LED: two copper, redstone, glass and red dye.
guide.electron.crafting.p3: Wrench: two iron, copper and a stick. Use to rotate 90 degrees; sneak-use rotates back. Disconnect first. Floor/ceiling components orient to the player; wall text starts upright.
guide.electron.protection.title: Protection before power
guide.electron.protection.subtitle: 07 / Diode and fuse
guide.electron.protection.p0: Put a 25 mA fuse in series with the supply. Accumulated overload blows it. It acts before the LED burns in the tested direct-supply circuit, but is not a substitute for a current-limiting resistor.
guide.electron.protection.p1: The silicon diode conducts from A to K; the silver band marks K. Its forward drop is about 0.7 V and its rated forward current is 50 mA. Reverse connection blocks current.
guide.electron.protection.p2: Fuse: one copper, iron nugget and glass, producing two. Diode: two copper, quartz and redstone. Damaged parts become scrap; check the fault before replacing.
guide.electron.protection.p3: Overload produces arcs and smoke. Severe overcurrent produces local popping particles and sound. Failed low-voltage components open the circuit without destroying nearby buildings.
guide.electron.precision.title: Crossings and precise connections
guide.electron.precision.subtitle: 08 / Bridges + magnifying visor
guide.electron.precision.p0: Install a bridge on the crossing face. L0 traces rise over existing conductors; for continuous upper-layer wiring, select L1 and bridge every supporting face. Routing avoids corner foot clearance and nodes cannot be placed there. Move existing corner connections before installing a bridge.
guide.electron.precision.p1: Ceramic feet replace the decorative parallel rails; colored runs are actual wires. Layers remain isolated unless you explicitly tap a wire. Saved bridge routes retain materials and connections. Sneak-use cutters to remove a bridge; unsupported runs return their paid wire length.
guide.electron.precision.p2: Visor recipe: two glass, copper, iron and leather. Use to equip, or put it in the head slot. Hold magnify (default Z) for 3x; sneaking gives 6x. The key can be changed in Controls.
guide.electron.precision.p3: Magnification slows aiming to help select fine wires. Release the key to return immediately. It is disabled in screens and does not blur the handbook.
guide.electron.scales.title: Three scales, shared electricity
guide.electron.scales.subtitle: 09 / Scale and ratings
guide.electron.scales.p0: Large circuits use cable and enclosure blocks such as distribution boxes, breakers, lamps and motors. Small circuits still use one device per block with fine wire. Both share the electrical network while retaining their wire sizes, ratings and models.
guide.electron.scales.p1: MOSFETs and relays let small control circuits switch power loads. DC converters change voltage according to input power and efficiency. Redstone cannot convert to or from electricity; an electrically actuated contact only blocks or passes existing redstone.
guide.electron.scales.p2: Integrated circuits are planned as small item parts placed, traced and soldered on player-designed PCBs. Resistors and logic ICs will not occupy individual world blocks. This system is not yet available.
guide.electron.scales.p3: Tooltips show the current model ratings. LEDs recommend 5–20 mA, corresponding to about 2.1–2.4 V forward drop. Use a 220 ohm series resistor with 5 V; a forward drop is not a direct supply rating.

guide.electron.series_parallel.title: Series, parallel and mixed circuits
guide.electron.series_parallel.subtitle: Wiring determines voltage and current; no mode selection
guide.electron.series_parallel.p0: Series: supply + → R1 → R2 → supply − forms one path. Both resistors carry the same current; resistance adds and voltage divides in proportion to resistance. Opening any point interrupts the loop.
guide.electron.series_parallel.p1: Parallel: connect both ends of R1 and R2 to the same pair of junctions. Branch voltages are nearly equal (wires have small resistance); each draws I = V/R, and branch currents add. Sharing only one end is not parallel.
guide.electron.series_parallel.p2: Tap an existing wire with the spool to make a branch. Crossing alone does not join wires; bridge layers remain isolated. Give each parallel LED branch its own series resistor. Opening one branch leaves the other working.
guide.electron.series_parallel.p3: For a mixed circuit, add a common series resistor ahead of parallel branches. Sneak-click a device with the meter for current; probe two terminals for voltage. The crank has 5 ohm internal resistance and wires drop voltage, so loaded voltage is below nominal 5 V.
guide.electron.timing.title: Button, capacitor and a fading LED
guide.electron.timing.subtitle: Stored energy and per-tick simulation; 20 ticks at normal speed
guide.electron.timing.p0: The momentary button is normally open. Right click with an empty hand to close it for 20 ticks, then reopen. Repeated clicks during a pulse do not extend it. It is a non-polar contact, not a voltage source or redstone output.
guide.electron.timing.p1: Fading lamp: crank + → button A; button B → capacitor +; capacitor − → supply −. Branch capacitor + through 220 ohm to LED +; LED − returns to capacitor −. Crank for energy, then press once. After release, the capacitor supplies the LED, which gradually dims.
guide.electron.timing.p2: The polarized capacitor is 100 mF (0.1 F), rated 10 V, with 1 ohm ESR and 1 Mohm leakage; its light stripe marks negative. Charging, discharging and reverse current are simulated. Sustained reversal, overvoltage or overcurrent damages it; failed capacitors are high impedance and store no energy.
guide.electron.timing.p3: Sneak-click with the meter for internal voltage and joules; positive current charges, negative current discharges. Saves retain voltage; unloaded or paused networks do not advance. Removed items are discharged. A 10k resistor pulls a logic input to VCC or GND; a button to the opposite rail prevents floating input after release.

guide.electron.power_modules.title: Energy storage and branching
guide.electron.power_modules.subtitle: Four battery pins · Two separate bus rails
guide.electron.power_modules.p0: 1  Batteries are crafted empty. Wire crank +/− to IN+/IN− to charge, and OUT+/OUT− to a complete load circuit. Recommended charging is 5 V, max 6 V / 250 mA. Output is 5 V with 5 Ω internal resistance and a 100 mA limit. Shorts collapse voltage and consume stored energy.
guide.electron.power_modules.p1: 2  Capacity is 200 J. The battery stores 80%% of actual input power; discharge efficiency is 90%%. Returns share a ground, so charging and output can work together. Backfeeding OUT does not charge it; looping output into input loses energy. Sneak-use with an empty hand toggles output only.
guide.electron.power_modules.p2: 3  Five panel lights show approximate charge. Use the multimeter for precise energy, output and charge readings. Survival inventory hides the live charge bar; creative mode may show it. Charge survives normal removal and replacement; modules do not stack. Paused or unloaded networks freeze. Sustained reverse polarity or overvoltage damages the module, leaving scrap.
guide.electron.power_modules.p3: 4  A1–A4 form one strip bus and B1–B4 another, isolated from each other. Adjacent same-bus pins have 0.002 Ω resistance. Use A as supply and B as return, with each parallel load connected across both. Each LED branch still needs its own series resistor.
guide.electron.redstone_switch.title: Electrically actuated redstone switch
guide.electron.redstone_switch.subtitle: Electricity moves the contact · Redstone stays redstone
guide.electron.redstone_switch.p0: 1  Electricity and redstone are independent systems; neither powers or converts into the other. This device only lets an electric circuit open or close a redstone path. Its electrical pins are a polarized +/− coil. The redstone path enters at the panel arrow tail and leaves at its tip, with no electrical pins.
guide.electron.redstone_switch.p1: 2  Supply the coil with 5 V, max 6 V; its resistance is 1 kΩ. It closes at 3.5 V and releases at 1.5 V with a 2-game-tick mechanical delay. Connect supply, electric switch and coil into a complete loop. The moving contact has an animation and sound.
guide.electron.redstone_switch.p2: 3  Feed an existing vanilla redstone signal into the arrow tail; connect redstone wiring or a redstone lamp to the tip. Closed contacts pass the original strength 0–15 unchanged; open contacts output 0. Electricity without redstone input always outputs 0, and redstone cannot supply electric wires.
guide.electron.redstone_switch.p3: 4  Mounting face and rotation determine input and output direction; redstone emits only from the arrow side. Loss of power releases the coil; network pauses or damage open contacts immediately. Sustained reverse polarity or overvoltage burns the device. Redstone gates still use redstone; wire gates still use electricity.

guide.electron.control.title: MOSFET and relay load control
guide.electron.control.subtitle: Small control circuits drive power loads
guide.electron.control.p0: 1  The N-channel MOSFET switches the low side: supply + → load → D, S → supply −. Connect the control signal to G and share its return with S. It switches on at 3 V gate-source and off at 1.5 V; gate-source max ±12 V, drain-source max 30 V / 2 A.
guide.electron.control.p1: 2  G has a 1 MΩ discharge path to S, with 0.08 Ω on resistance between D/S and a body diode from S to D. A wire logic gate Y can drive G without carrying the load current. Reversed wiring or excessive ratings can damage it.
guide.electron.control.p2: 3  Wire relay COIL+/− to a 5 V control circuit and COM/NO in series with the load. Coil and contacts are electrically isolated, so the load may use another supply. Pull-in is 3.5 V, release 1.5 V, with 2 ticks delay; contacts max 30 V / 2 A. This relay switches electricity only.
guide.electron.control.p3: 4  Motors model armature resistance, back EMF, inertia and shaft load. Use to select free, loaded or locked shaft; locking increases current. Add a breaker, use cable for the power loop and watch startup or stall with the meter. This release simulates shaft loads; it does not yet drive external pumps or conveyors.
guide.electron.conversion.title: DC step-up and step-down
guide.electron.conversion.subtitle: Voltage changes; input power still limits output
guide.electron.conversion.p0: 1  Small circuits use five fixed-output modules. Buck outputs 3.3 / 5 / 12 V accept 4.5–30 / 7–30 / 14–30 V respectively. Boost outputs 12 / 24 V accept 2.5–10 / 2.5–20 V. Each model accepts an input range; individual input/output pairs are not separate devices.
guide.electron.conversion.p1: 2  Fixed models have no voltage-setting interface. Craft and replace the module to change its nominal output; sneak-use only toggles output. The future PCB stage will combine small power ICs, inductors, capacitors and feedback resistors by soldering. Adjustable ICs will derive their setting from feedback parts, not a free voltage entry.
guide.electron.conversion.p2: 3  This averaged model has 85%% efficiency and a 0.5 J buffer. Input limits are 300 mA for boost and 500 mA for buck; output is at most 500 mA and is further limited by actual input power. Undervoltage stops charging; overvoltage or reverse polarity may damage it. Inadequate power causes droop or pulsing. Measure actual output with the meter.
guide.electron.conversion.p3: 4  Sustained reverse polarity, excessive input voltage or overvoltage forced into the output damages the converter. Removal discharges its small buffer; world saves preserve it and pauses/unloading freeze it. Redstone remains independent and cannot replace an electrical supply.
guide.electron.distribution.title: Low-voltage distribution
guide.electron.distribution.subtitle: Cable, branching, protection and loads
guide.electron.distribution.p0: 1  Craft the 24 V hand-crank DC generator. One crank per second adds 50 J; capacity is 2000 J with 4 Ω internal resistance and a 2 A output limit. Power devices have separate enclosure models and a creative tab. They connect to small devices through actual electrical terminals.
guide.electron.distribution.p1: 2  Single-core cable has 0.002 Ω per block and a 5 A rating; lay supply and return separately. Fine wire has 0.02 Ω per block and a 250 mA rating; sustained overload burns it. Color only labels a wire. The 128-run world limit is removed; 32-block runs and the 256-node per-network solver budget remain.
guide.electron.distribution.p2: 3  Connect supply + → 1 A breaker → box bus A; supply − → bus B. A/B are isolated, with four terminals per rail for branches. The engineering lamp is a 24 V / 2.4 W load whose brightness follows power. Connect the motor on another branch and control it with a MOSFET or relay.
guide.electron.distribution.p3: The bulkhead lamp uses 24 V / 2.4 W; the yard lamp uses 24 V / 6 W. Both mount in any direction and produce vanilla light only when powered. Above 28 V they can fail; use suitable step-down modules and protection. The crusher, centrifuge, kiln and fabricator also use 24 V; see Powered processing.

guide.electron.power_grid.title: Power grids and plants
guide.electron.power_grid.subtitle: 240 V rectified bus > 24 V loads > 5 V control
guide.electron.power_grid.p0: Build the specified plant, fuel thermal/nuclear controllers and fill their dedicated tanks. Hydro requires flowing water at the turbine; wind outputs through its base cabinet. Lightning collectors use real strikes. See high-voltage ratings for each formed plant.
guide.electron.power_grid.p1: Route generator +/− through separate power cables to tower A/B rails, then the receiving service IN. Service OUT feeds station IN; station OUT supplies 24 V loads. The service inlet creates no energy. The station runs at 92% efficiency.
guide.electron.power_grid.p2: Aerial wire costs its curved length. Higher voltage requires greater clearance for overhead and vertical spans. Insufficient clearance causes leakage, arcing and shock. See Arcs, overheating and shock for distances and fault handling.
guide.electron.power_grid.p3: Use the multimeter for live readings. Nuclear generation stops without coolant and a hot reactor shuts down. This is an energy-accounted rectified DC model, without AC phases, radiation or fuel reprocessing.
guide.electron.mechanics.title: Motors, shafts and platforms
guide.electron.mechanics.subtitle: Connect along the central output axis
guide.electron.mechanics.p0: The motor face has a central output shaft. Place aligned shafts and a rotating platform along it. All three axes work; straight transmissions scan up to 16 blocks.
guide.electron.mechanics.p1: Use a plain block on the platform to mount one item. Sneak-use with an empty hand to retrieve it. Breaking the platform returns the mounted item. Containers and data-bearing items are rejected.
guide.electron.mechanics.p2: A mounted block adds motor load. Breaking the shaft or stopping the motor stops the platform. The mounted item is a rotating display; it does not execute world-block behavior or move players.
guide.electron.mechanics.p3: Each conductor color is a separate item. Using a spool in air ends the run instead of changing color. Lamps need actual power, and shaders need the appropriate light mapping or emissive materials; unpowered states stay dark.

guide.electron.multiblocks.title: Multiblocks and towers
guide.electron.multiblocks.subtitle: Complete structure → automatic formation → connect power
guide.electron.multiblocks.p0: Transmission towers use 3–63 lattice sections, a terminal head and solid footings; completion automatically forms the tapered truss and crossarms. Wind turbines use separate tubular masts and a base cabinet; see the wind chapter.
guide.electron.multiblocks.p1: Connect cables at the porcelain insulators on the crossarms: four taps on the left A rail and four on the right B rail. Click a copper tip, then another tower. Central service pins accept supported downleads. Suspended cable costs its curved length.
guide.electron.multiblocks.p2: Thermal plants need a 7×7 foundation and workshop-built modules; nuclear plants need a 36×36 site and dedicated cooling. See the build chapters. Place the hydro turbine in flowing water. Substations retain a 3×3 foundation and four casings.
guide.electron.multiblocks.p3: Complete structures form automatically. Breaking a part restores the others and pauses automatic formation. Use a wrench with the missing parts in your inventory to repair; occupied cells are never overwritten. Sneak-use dismantles intentionally. Repair preserves stored fuel and water; a replacement tank starts empty.
guide.electron.high_voltage.title: Generation and fixed ratios
guide.electron.high_voltage.subtitle: 11 / 6.6 / 24 kV > 240 V > 24 V > control
guide.electron.high_voltage.p0: Formed thermal generators output 11 kV, hydro 6.6 kV and nuclear turbine generators 24 kV. Craft the matching fixed-ratio station to reach 240 V, then a normal station for 24 V. Winding ratios cannot be changed for free. Wind and lightning collectors include a 240 V output stage.
guide.electron.high_voltage.p1: Stations accept 75%-110% of nominal input with 92% efficiency. Actual input power charges the finite buffer before output can supply loads. High voltage is not unlimited energy. Power and fuel are accounted separately. Networks use a DC equivalent with real-world-inspired voltage ratings, without three-phase simulation.
guide.electron.high_voltage.p2: Lightning is a brief pulse. The collector records a 300 MV / 30 kA event peak. Its 0.1 pF equivalent capture branch and 2/3 conversion efficiency recover up to 3 kJ per strike, with a 4 kJ total buffer and 240 V output. Meter readings include the last peak and captured energy. Each actual strike is counted once.
guide.electron.high_voltage.p3: Fuel heat drives the nuclear plant. Cooling loss trips generation but residual heat needs cooling; persistent loss can cause a pressure accident. Legacy compact thermal, nuclear and wind plants must be rebuilt. Match high-voltage outputs to suitable substations.

guide.electron.industrial_build.title: Thermal plant assembly
guide.electron.industrial_build.subtitle: Workbench → modules → 7×7 plant
guide.electron.industrial_build.p0: Craft six workbench modules and place them individually on level supports in a 3×2 rectangle facing the same way. All six are required to open it. Removing one disables it, preserves the other modules and returns stored materials. Add circuit parts and metals, select a module and assemble.
guide.electron.industrial_build.p1: Place the controller at the centre of the front edge. Relative to its service face, right is +X and rear is −Z. Foundation: X=−3…3, Z=−6…0. Boiler (0,0,−4), turbine (2,0,−3), alternator (2,0,−1), condenser (−2,0,−4).
guide.electron.industrial_build.p2: Console (0,0,-1), valve (0,1,-4), tank (-2,0,-1), solid intake (-3,1,-2), ash outlet (-3,1,-4), pipe inlet (-3,0,-1). Leave eight cells of headroom. Place coal and ash chests against the respective marked outward faces. Top hoppers feed coal; bottom hoppers extract ash.
guide.electron.industrial_build.p3: Low water stops generation. A hot dry plant trips and alarms, but residual heat remains. Refill and cool before restarting. Prolonged cooling loss can damage the plant and cause a bounded steam-pressure explosion affecting nearby blocks.
guide.electron.fluids.title: Reservoirs, pipes and pumps
guide.electron.fluids.subtitle: Finite storage; pumping consumes real electricity
guide.electron.fluids.p0: Feedwater tanks hold 16 buckets; nuclear reservoirs hold 256. Use a water bucket to add 1000 mB or an empty bucket to withdraw one bucket. Visible level follows actual storage; breaking a tank discards its contents.
guide.electron.fluids.p1: A 24 V / 2.4 W pump transfers up to one bucket per second. Rear intake accepts a tank or vanilla water body; front connects to pipes. All pumps share the withdrawal ledger. At 1000 mB per source cell, a finite body loses its whole top layer only when that layer is paid for. The intake must stay submerged. Partial consumption is saved.
guide.electron.fluids.p2: A verified connected layer of at least 1024 water cells is renewable. Smaller ponds drain by layers, even when they would normally regenerate as vanilla infinite pools. Multiple pumps drain faster. Unloaded boundaries or search-budget overflow pause intake. Contained water uses vanilla animated sprites and biome tint without placing world fluid.
guide.electron.fluids.p3: Internal plant tanks reject buckets and direct pump feeds. Connect to their fixed pipe inlets. External reservoirs still accept buckets and require a powered pump for delivery. Pipes and tanks use vanilla water textures for stored fluid; they do not create world water blocks.
guide.electron.nuclear_site.title: 36×36 nuclear facility
guide.electron.nuclear_site.subtitle: Containment, turbine hall, condenser and reservoir
guide.electron.nuclear_site.p0: From the front controller build a 36×36 smooth-stone foundation: X=-15…20, Z=-35…0, with 21 cells of headroom. Offsets rotate with facing. Place a three-high shielding ring at X=-8…2, Z=-25…-15. The basin is sealed. The former control room is replaced by an external service yard.
guide.electron.nuclear_site.p1: Vessel (-3,0,-20), rod drive (-3,1,-20), valve (-3,3,-20); turbines (7,0,-7)/(10,0,-7), alternator (7,0,-3), condenser (6,0,-15), external console (16,0,-3), rod intake (20,1,-3), spent outlet (20,1,-5).
guide.electron.nuclear_site.p2: Tank (-14,0,-5) receives water only through the pipe inlet (-14,0,-4). Powered pumps draw from world water or external reservoirs. Only finished fuel rods are accepted: crush uranium, centrifuge, sinter and fabricate using electricity. Eastern chests feed rods and receive spent rods. The console accepts neither items nor buckets.
guide.electron.nuclear_site.p3: Fuel and water are finite; a full output prevents rod replacement. Decay heat still needs cooling after shutdown. Water loss trips and alarms; excessive temperature causes damage and a pressure explosion with a mushroom-shaped smoke plume. Actual failure triggers the effect; normal shutdown does not explode. Typed ports are not interchangeable. A wrench can repair missing paid structure.
guide.electron.wind_and_wires.title: Wind, hanging drops and breakout sockets
guide.electron.wind_and_wires.subtitle: Tubular mast / base output / two fixed anchors
guide.electron.wind_and_wires.p0: Place a wind base cabinet, stack 6–63 mast sections, then add the turbine controller. Leave a roughly ten-cell rotor sweep. It automatically forms a white tapered tower with three blades. Connect OUT+/OUT− at the base; top contacts are removed.
guide.electron.wind_and_wires.p1: Wire and cable can hang vertically between aligned device contacts, screw terminals or wall ports. Free nodes cannot anchor a hanging end. Maximum length is 64 cells, charged at real length. Solids and water may not intersect the run.
guide.electron.wind_and_wires.p2: Removing either anchor disconnects and refunds the drop. Horizontal suspended cables still require transmission towers. Heavy insulation tapers near contacts. Use a breakout socket to split two isolated buses and fine wire for precision devices, respecting current ratings.
guide.electron.wind_and_wires.p3: A formed collector can redirect strikes within 64 horizontal cells whose original target is below its tip. One eligible tower is chosen randomly. Only a real strike charges it. This radius is a gameplay rule, not a real lightning-protection claim.
message.electron.wind_base_output: Wire the tower-base cabinet: use to open/close, sneak-use to switch power
tooltip.electron.low_socket: Isolated A/B buses / four taps each / rated 5 A
guide.electron.faults.title: Arcs, overheating and shock
guide.electron.faults.subtitle: Isolate power before repair; sound comes from the discharge
guide.electron.faults.p0: Overhead and anchored vertical conductors check real solid surfaces, water and other energized spans. Clearance is 0.45 cells at 240 V, 1.2 at 6.6 kV, 1.6 at 11 kV and 2.4 at 24 kV. These are gameplay distances. Surface-insulated wire does not discharge into its mounting plate.
guide.electron.faults.p1: Leakage is a passive energy-consuming solver branch. Shorts, current limiting, wire heating, fuses and breakers remain part of the circuit. Branching blue-white arcs, falling sparks and local flashes mark faults. Hot insulation sizzles and smokes before glowing fragments and a melt snap.
guide.electron.faults.p2: Approaching a high-voltage span or touching a high-voltage fine wire can create a shock path. Actual fault current is required for damage, capped at one hit per second with brief slowness. Ground strikes create a local hazard, wider in water. Creative/spectator players are exempt; unpowered wires produce no sustained arcs.
guide.electron.faults.p3: Pressure accidents have distinct machine, boiler and reactor effects. Reactor failure produces expanding dust, a rising stem and mushroom-shaped smoke for about 20 seconds; boiler smoke lasts about 9 seconds. Sound originates at the boiler or vessel. Cloud size is separate from physical damage; blast strengths remain 3 for thermal and 5 for nuclear plants.

guide.electron.processing.title: Powered processing
guide.electron.processing.subtitle: Real power > separation > sintering > fabrication
guide.electron.processing.p0: All four machines use 24 V, operating at 18–30 V: crusher 16 W, centrifuge 20 W, kiln 24 W, fabricator 12 W. Connect both power terminals and load inputs. Power loss or full outputs pause work. Start with the hand-powered DC generator before expanding renewable supply.
guide.electron.processing.p1: One raw uranium makes two crushed ore. The centrifuge separates two crushed ore into one concentrate plus one tailings. The kiln sinters one concentrate into one pellet. Fabricate four pellets plus one cladding into a fuel rod. Craft cladding with two iron and one copper ingot. Legacy shortcut recipes are removed.
guide.electron.processing.p2: The crusher handles raw iron and copper; the kiln converts their dust into ingots at 1:1. The fabricator presses two iron ingots into one plate or winds two copper ingots into one coil. Plates and coils feed precision plant components beyond nuclear fuel.
guide.electron.processing.p3: Top/side hoppers insert ingredients; bottom hoppers extract outputs only. Paid work is saved. Removing or changing incompatible ingredients resets the batch. Completion checks and consumes inputs atomically. Overvoltage or reversed polarity can damage the machine; use appropriate protection.

guide.electron.pcb_design.title: Dense PCB design
guide.electron.pcb_design.subtitle: Parts tray, zoom, copper layers and custom ports
guide.electron.pcb_design.p0: The design station plots masks; the assembly station follows already-manufactured copper. It cannot redesign a gold-finished board. Default grid: 32x24; size presets extend to 128x96, with up to 256 packages and individually routed pads.
guide.electron.pcb_design.p1: Filter the tray by category/name; arrows or wheel change pages. Drag parts and press R to rotate. Drag empty space, MMB or Space to pan; wheel zooms at the pointer, F fits. Select or Shift-drag a region across all layers; top-right buttons or Ctrl+C/X/V copy, move and place. Delete removes; Ctrl+Z/Y undo/redo.
guide.electron.pcb_design.p2: Layers selects one to four copper layers; the L button changes the active layer. Click successive nodes to route, holding Shift for the other elbow direction. Same-layer crossings join; different layers remain isolated until a plated via connects them. Outline milling cannot split the substrate.
guide.electron.pcb_design.p3: Select VCC/GND/A/B/Y/Z, then a board-edge pad; six external socket contacts stay fixed. Example arrows choose NOT, half adder, pixel or counter. The calculator button remains. Region edits preserve outline and ports; boundary-crossing copper stays behind and needs reconnection after moving. Invalid or overlapping edits are rejected atomically.
guide.electron.pcb_process.title: PCB fabrication by area
guide.electron.pcb_process.subtitle: Substrate, copper layers, reagents, drilling and energy
guide.electron.pcb_process.p0: Area units U=ceil(width*height/768); process units M=U*layers. Exposure consumes M laminate sheets and one patterned mask. Plotting consumes M films and M black dyes. Milled cutouts do not refund the original sheet; legacy small boards cost at least one unit.
guide.electron.pcb_process.p1: Drilling, etching, masking and immersion gold each consume M matching reagents. Wet stages produce the same number of spent cartridges. Base process energy is multiplied by M, plus 2 J per via. Limited input power means larger multilayer boards take longer and spend more energy.
guide.electron.pcb_process.p2: Assembly consumes one matching gold-finished board, the actual packages and one solder unit per 32 pads. Energy is 40M + 12 per package + 0.5 per copper edge + 4 per via, in joules. Page through the tray and feed more than one stack in batches. Reserved materials persist and are returned on cancel.
guide.electron.pcb_process.p3: Place a socket at the anchor corner and complete a horizontal carrier of ceil(width/32) by ceil(height/24) tiles using extensions. Incomplete support rejects insertion; removing support stops the circuit. Installed packages, vias and top copper are visible. Use onboard inputs with an empty hand; sneak-use blank board space to remove it.
guide.electron.automation.title: Level interlocks and emergency lighting
guide.electron.automation.subtitle: Powered sensing > isolated contacts > load control
guide.electron.automation.p0: Level and temperature sensors use 5 V; COM/NO is an isolated contact, not an energy source. Contacts handle 30 V / 2 A and can switch pump supply or PCB signals. Missing target, power loss and damage open the contact.
guide.electron.automation.p1: The level switch senses one immediately adjacent tank/fluid reservoir. Default refill closes below 25% and opens at 75%; use to select minimum 25%/75% interlocks. Multiple targets open it rather than selecting an arbitrary one.
guide.electron.automation.p2: Place the temperature interlock next to a plant core. Presets open above 60, 90 or 120°C and reset 5°C below. It switches an external electrical circuit and supplements the plant protection. Use its contacts for alarms or load shedding.
guide.electron.automation.p3: The emergency lamp charges from 24 V into 200 J storage. Lamp: 1.2 W; charging: 6 W at 90% efficiency. Power loss switches to finite battery energy until empty. Crafted lamps start empty; removal preserves stored energy. It uses vanilla block light.

guide.electron.plug_power.title: Outlets, strips and cords
guide.electron.plug_power.subtitle: Supply, distribute, then match appliance voltage
guide.electron.plug_power.p0: Generator -> fixed substation -> 240 V protected inlet -> wall outlet. Existing wires feed IN+/IN-. One jacket contains separate outgoing and return conductors. Use the cord on a socket, then on an appliance, strip or adapter. Outlets cannot create energy.
guide.electron.plug_power.p1: Outlets have one socket; strips have three. Strips preserve voltage. The crafted workshop adapter accepts 180–264 V and supplies 24 V, up to about 48 W at 88% efficiency. Put it before a low-voltage strip. Lamps, pumps, motors, processing machines and the PCB bench accept cords. Direct 240 V can still destroy a 24 V appliance.
guide.electron.plug_power.p2: Each prefabricated cord supports up to 12 routed blocks on a floor or bench, including vertical end drops. Strips and cords are rated 2.5 A; sustained overload trips or burns them. Appliances accept one incoming cord. Sneak-use a cord on a device to unplug and recover one lead; breaking an end also returns it.
guide.electron.plug_power.p3: Ratings are documented here instead of printed onto appliance models: engineering/bulkhead lamps 24 V 2.4 W, yard lamp 24 V 6 W, emergency lamp 24 V; crusher 16 W, centrifuge 20 W, kiln 24 W, fabricator 12 W, all at 24 V; PCB exposure/drilling/etching/masking/gold finishing also use 24 V. Measure live values with a multimeter. Open a wiring cabinet, connect, then close; closing does not disconnect power.

guide.electron.digital_display.title: Single-PCB gate calculator
guide.electron.digital_display.subtitle: Inputs, binary arithmetic and decimal readout on one board
guide.electron.digital_display.p0: The teaching board has two 0–9 dials, an add/subtract switch, 52 basic gates, a minus bar and two numeric displays: 58 packages total. One 80x88 four-layer PCB performs the calculation. Its 3x4 carrier provides support, with no separate arithmetic controller.
guide.electron.digital_display.p1: Use dial A/B to increment; sneak-use decrements. The switch selects addition when off, subtraction when on. Wait for gate propagation; results range from -9 to 18. XOR, AND, OR and NOT implement carry, complement, magnitude and decimal correction. Displays only decode their four input bits.
guide.electron.digital_display.p2: Internal connections are editable copper and vias; external 5 V power uses fine wire. Removing power/support, moving pads or shorting nets affects computation. Digital packages operate at 4.5–5.5 V, with logic outputs rated 20 mA each and powered by actual supply rails.
guide.electron.digital_display.p3: Numeric modules show 0–F; SIGN high lights the minus bar. Existing numeric panels can still be tiled. Use pixel panels for arbitrary patterns, text or animations; see Pixels and RGB. The main-mod sample has no dependency on the separate vanilla-redstone calculator mod.
pcb.electron.support_required: This PCB needs a %s×%s horizontal carrier. Complete it with carrier extensions beside the socket.
pcb.electron.board_controls: Use the onboard dial/switch with an empty hand. Sneak-use a blank area to remove the PCB.
pcb_ui.electron.help_4: Click to add/remove a plated through via. Layers join only at vias.
pcb_ui.electron.help_5: Choose VCC/GND/A/B/Y/Z, then click the board edge to place its contact.
display.electron.pixel_help: VCC/GND power; DATA bits, CLK rising edge shifts, LATCH rising edge refreshes, CLEAR high resets.

guide.electron.pcb_logic.title: PCB logic and sequential parts
guide.electron.pcb_logic.subtitle: Combinational logic, storage and clocks use real supply rails
guide.electron.pcb_logic.p0: The complete basic set is AND, OR, NOT, XOR, NAND, NOR, XNOR and BUFFER. Standard pins are VCC/GND/A/B/Y; NOT and BUFFER use only A. Gates have two-tick propagation delay; floating, unpowered and intermediate voltages are not valid binary inputs.
guide.electron.pcb_logic.p1: D flip-flops sample D on rising CLK. Reset a T flip-flop first; with T=1 each rising edge toggles Q, dividing frequency by two. SR latches set at S=1 and reset at R=1; both high is invalid. Sequential chips power up unknown: reset or sample known input.
guide.electron.pcb_logic.p2: Counter pins: VCC/GND/CLK/RESET/Q0/Q1/Q2/Q3. After reset, rising CLK counts modulo 16. Shift-register pins: VCC/GND/D/CLK/Q0/Q1/Q2/Q3. Rising CLK moves D into Q0 and old Q0 into Q1; four known bits establish all outputs. Power loss clears volatile state; save/reload retains state and edge history.
guide.electron.pcb_logic.p3: Use the arrow beside Example to select NOT, half adder, pixel or counter, then load. On the counter board, switch RESET to 1 then 0 with a stable 5 V supply; the onboard clock advances the display. Logic packages draw about 0.5 mA, displays 5 mA. No direct redstone connection. Use the oscillator to change clock rate; buffers and multiplexers organize shared signals.
guide.electron.pcb_pixels.title: Pixels and RGB
guide.electron.pcb_pixels.subtitle: Write every pixel directly, with no fixed numeric font
guide.electron.pcb_pixels.p0: The RGB package has VCC/GND/R/G/B pins. Three independent binary color inputs produce eight states. Insufficient power or floating inputs blank it. At 5 V its base draw is about 1 mA, plus 3 mA per illuminated channel.
guide.electron.pcb_pixels.p1: The miniature matrix has 8x8 pixels and VCC/GND/DATA/CLK/LATCH/CLEAR pins. Send 64 bits in row-major order, starting at the top left. Stabilize DATA before raising CLK. A rising LATCH edge refreshes the screen; CLEAR=1 erases both shift register and frame.
guide.electron.pcb_pixels.p2: Coplanar pixel panels with matching rotation form one rectangular display, up to 256 tiles. Each tile contributes 8x8 pixels. Send a complete row-major frame of tile_count*64 bits. Edge contacts share all six electrical signals. A 2x2 panel needs 256 bits for a 16x16 image.
guide.electron.pcb_pixels.p3: Select Pixel demo with the arrow beside Example, then load. Four switches left to right: DATA/CLK/LATCH/CLEAR. Set data, pulse clock and finally raise latch. A powered map example is included. Each tile draws about 2 mA at 5 V plus 0.3 mA per lit pixel; power loss clears volatile buffers.
pcb_ui.electron.help_6: Drag the canvas to pan. Wheel zooms at the cursor; F fits the board.
